name: Lumen Adaptive Base Layer
description:
A close-fitting long-sleeve base layer in a smooth four-way stretch fabric that looks at first like a high-end athletic shirt — matte charcoal or slate grey, minimal seaming, a low crew neck. It fits like a second skin without compressing, and the fabric manages temperature actively: a network of phase-change micro-capsules in the weave absorbs excess body heat when you're warm and releases it when you cool down, keeping the wearer in a narrow comfort band across a wide range of ambient temperatures. The effect is subtle — you notice it as an absence of discomfort rather than a positive sensation.

Lumen is a Tier 3 brand that found its market between athletic performance and everyday wear. This shirt is popular with couriers, cycle commuters, people with physically demanding jobs who also have to look presentable afterward, and anyone who moves between the climate-controlled interior zones and the unregulated temperature swings of the outer corridor. It layers smoothly under anything. The tech is quiet and functional — there's no display, no app, no connectivity. It just works.
functionality: Passive thermal regulation via phase-change micro-capsule weave. No power source required. Maintains wearer comfort across a 25-degree ambient temperature range without active heating or cooling.
what_it_says: You move a lot and you've thought about what you need. You're not interested in showing off the tech — you just want it to work.
worn_by: people who run cold or hot
story_hooks: A Lumen base layer recovered from a the Gray Zone casualty shows no signs of wear despite reportedly being in continuous use for two years — the phase-change material is somehow intact, which shouldn't be possible.
Lumen's thermal regulation technology was originally licensed from a TESSERA biophysics division patent — and TESSERA's lawyers have just sent a notice of license termination.
A character wearing a Lumen base layer is the only person in a group to survive prolonged exposure in a failing climate-control zone — and they're not sure whether to tell anyone why.

physical_description.visual_profile: A sleek, minimalist long-sleeve base layer that hugs the torso like a second skin without visual bulk. The matte charcoal or slate grey finish reads clean and understated—athletic in intent but refined enough for professional contexts. Low crew neck sits just below the collarbone. Minimal visible seaming creates an almost seamless appearance. The garment moves with the body rather than against it.
physical_description.fit: Slim, form-fitting without compression. Four-way stretch allows full range of motion. Sits close enough to layer invisibly under jackets, vests, or armor plating without bunching. Sleeves taper gently to the wrist.
physical_description.primary_material: High-performance four-way stretch synth-blend weave embedded with phase-change micro-capsules. Smooth surface, technical but non-reflective.
physical_description.texture: Soft, matte finish. Slightly tactile—smooth but with subtle micro-grip that prevents sliding. The weave is tight enough to be invisible at arm's length; up close, you can see the uniform knit structure and faint shimmer of integrated capsule network.
physical_description.color_scheme: Matte charcoal grey or slate grey. Neutral, universal. No patterns, no branding visible on the body—minimal aesthetic footprint.
physical_description.closures: None. Pullover design with elasticated crew neck and wrist cuffs.
distinctive_features: Embedded phase-change micro-capsules throughout the weave—thermal regulation without electronics
Nearly invisible seaming; virtually seamless construction at shoulders and sides
Four-way stretch fabric allows unrestricted movement
Minimal branding—Lumen logo only on inner neckline tag
Temperature-adaptive function: absorbs heat when warm, releases when cool
Ideal layering piece—creates no bulk under outerwear
physical_description.tier_indicator: Tier 3 functional. Quality material and proven tech, but accessible pricing. Signals practical investment rather than luxury.
physical_description.cultural_context: Worn by couriers, cycle commuters, warehouse workers, medical techs, anyone with physically demanding work who needs to transition seamlessly between environments. Suggests someone who values function over fashion, who moves between climate zones regularly, who treats their gear as tools rather than status symbols.
physical_description.condition_typical: Broken-in but well-maintained. Shows minor wear at collar and cuffs from repeated use. No visible pilling. Maintains structural integrity over years of heavy wear.
